Class HashSetMultimap<K,V>

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.collect.HashSetMultimap<K,V>
Type Parameters:
K - the key type
V - the value type
All Implemented Interfaces:
Multimap<K,V>, SetMultimap<K,V>, Serializable
public final class HashSetMultimap<K,V> extends Object implements Serializable
A modifiable set multimap backed by a HashMap from each key to a HashSet of its values. Its keys and values must have consistent equals and hashCode methods.
  • It iterates over its keys, and over the values of a key, in no particular order.
  • It rejects null keys and values, but querying it with null, as in containsKey(null), is allowed.
  • Its views are live, and its iterators support Iterator.remove(). The collections of Multimap.asMap() do not support adding values: add them through Multimap.get(Object) or Multimap.put(K, V).
  • Its iterators fail fast, on a best-effort basis, when it changes while they iterate, outside of their own remove().
  • It is serializable if all its keys and values are.
  • It is not thread-safe.
Since:
0.1.2

    • equals

      public boolean equals(@Nullable Object o)
      Description copied from interface: Multimap
      Returns whether another object is a multimap with the same keys and values. Two multimaps are equal when their Multimap.asMap() views are, so a ListMultimap equals another one with the same values in the same order, and a SetMultimap another one with the same values in any order. A list multimap never equals a set multimap, unless both are empty.
      Specified by:
      equals in interface Multimap<K,V>
      Overrides:
      equals in class Object
      Parameters:
      o - the object to compare with
      Returns:
      true if o is an equal multimap
